Overview.Name: Sujatha Kulkarni
Overview.Goal: Looking better (appearance), Feeling energetic & confident, Preventing/reversing health issues, Mental wellbeing & stress reduction

Early_Morning (optional): Option 1: Warm water (200 ml) + methi seeds water (1 tsp soaked)
Option 2: Warm water (200 ml) + soaked almonds (6 nos)
Option 3: Warm water (200 ml) + fruit (100 g)
Breakfast: Option 1: Idli (2 small) + sambar (150 g) + coconut chutney (20 g)
Option 2: Vegetable upma (80 g) with mixed vegetables (60 g) + curd (100 g)
Option 3: Moong dal dosa (2 small) + tomato chutney (30 g)
Lunch: Option 1: Plain rice (140 g) + dal (150 g) + vegetable curry (120 g) + salad (50 g)
Option 2: Millet rice (140 g) + sambar (180 g) + vegetable fry (100 g) + curd (100 g)
Option 3: Curd rice (140 g) + vegetable curry (150 g) + salad (50 g)
Evening_Snack: Option 1: Roasted makhana (30 g) + green tea (200 ml)
Option 2: Puffed rice (30 g) + roasted chana (25 g) + cucumber (50 g)
Dinner: Option 1: Vegetable soup (250 ml) + paneer curry (120 g) + salad (50 g)
Option 2: Mixed vegetable stir-fry (180 g) + curd (120 g)
Option 3: Dal (180 g) + vegetable curry (150 g) (lightest option)

Notes_and_Tips: For diabetes: avoid sugar, sweets, and sweetened drinks; keep rice portions controlled.
For hypertension: keep salt very moderate; avoid pickles, papad, and packaged foods.
For gluten allergy: avoid wheat/chapati; choose rice, millets, and dal-based options.
Avoid soy in all forms (soy chunks, soy sauce, tofu).
Aim for a 10–15 minute walk after lunch/dinner if possible to support sugar control.
Consistency improves appearance and energy: keep meals simple and repeatable.
